chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa, do you know why I chose you with My Speech among My creation?' He said: 'O Lord, and why was that?' So Allah, Blessed and High, revealed to him: 'O Musa, I turned My servants over (examined them) and did not find among them anyone more humble to Me with his self than you, O Musa. Indeed, when you pray, you place your cheek upon the dust,' or he said: 'upon the ground.'

key_terms.أَذَلَّ لِي نَفْساً: More humble to Me with his self

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah choose Prophet Musa for direct speech?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni uses this hadith to illustrate the principle of *takhassus* (special selection) based on *tawadu* (humility), where God chose Musa not for innate superiority but for his unique self-abasement. The imagery of placing the cheek on the dust during prayer (*sujud*) serves as a physical manifestation of the heart's submission, a key theme in Shia spiritual ethics linking outward ritual to inward state. This narrative reinforces the idea that divine proximity is earned through the eradication of ego, a concept central to the station of the Prophets and Imams.
